candidate.blueprint_locator: Physiological Adaptation, Pathophysiology and Illness Management, printed p.48 / PDF p.51: identify pathophysiology related to acute or chronic conditions and apply knowledge of client pathophysiology to illness management
candidate.educational_objective: Explain that unabsorbed carbohydrate can be fermented by colonic bacteria, producing acidic stool in carbohydrate malabsorption.

options.A: Unabsorbed carbohydrate reaches the colon and is fermented by intestinal bacteria into acidic products
options.B: Excess absorbed carbohydrate is converted directly into gastric hydrochloric acid
options.C: Bile flow is completely obstructed, preventing bilirubin from reaching the intestine
options.D: Dietary protein is lost through the kidneys and acidifies the stool

candidate.rationale: NCBI StatPearls explains that when carbohydrates are not adequately absorbed, the remaining carbohydrate can reach the colon and undergo bacterial fermentation. Excessive fermentation in carbohydrate malabsorption is associated with acidic stool, flatulence, and bloating. Therefore A best explains the finding. The other options describe unrelated gastric, biliary, or renal processes and do not account for fermentation-related stool acidity.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Unabsorbed carbohydrate reaching the colon undergoes bacterial fermentation, which can produce acidic stool in carbohydrate malabsorption.
candidate.source_locator: Carbohydrate malabsorption section: carbohydrates remaining unabsorbed are fermented in the colon by bacterial degradation; signs of excessive bacterial fermentation in carbohydrate malabsorption include acidic stool, flatulence, and bloating
candidate.source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI), StatPearls
candidate.source_version_date: StatPearls 2026 edition; current NCBI page accessed 2026-08-17
candidate.stem: An infant with suspected carbohydrate malabsorption has chronic watery stools that are acidic. Which process best explains the acidic stool?
